name: Lublin Voivodeship
summary_text: Lubelskie carried a voivodeship-level "LGBT-free" resolution from 2020 until its 20 September 2021 repeal under European Commission funding pressure. Its municipality of Świdnik (population ~40,000) was the first local authority in all of Poland to adopt an anti-LGBT resolution (March 2019, "against homopropaganda, LGBT ideology and the early sexualisation of Polish children"), and its deputy council chair explained the act explicitly as opposition to Warsaw's LGBT+ Declaration signed a month earlier. Świdnik became the template copied by roughly 100 authorities nationwide. The resolution is now formally gone, but as with other eastern voivodeships the repeal was coerced rather than converted—the underlying civic mobilisation that produced Poland's first-ever anti-LGBT charter persists as a de facto signal. No march violence or ban is documented at the voivodeship scale beyond the general resolution-era hostility. Score of 0.45 sits 0.07 below the national 0.52. Above Subcarpathian (0.42), which additionally produced a mayoral march ban and held out until 2025, and above Podlaskie (0.44), where the 2019 coordinated mass assault adds a violence dimension absent in Lublin. Below Małopolska (0.48), which pairs its resolution history with Kraków's clearly positive institutional trajectory.

sources.title: Poland’s LGBT-free zones and global anti-gender campaigns
sources.claim_summary: Social-science institute publication on Poland's LGBT-free zones: Swidnik (Lublin county, ~40,000 people) became the country's first 'LGBT-free' municipality in March 2019, a non-binding resolution against 'homosexual propaganda' and 'LGBT ideology' that withdrew support for equality organisations - explicitly framed by its deputy council chair as opposition to Warsaw's February 2019 LGBT+ charter; with ruling-party and Catholic-clergy backing, over 80 municipalities and four voivodeships had similar declarations by March 2020, mapped by activists' Atlas of Hate and lobbied by the Ordo Iuris institute.

sources.title: This Could Be the Beginning of the End for Poland’s “LGBT-Free” Zones | Them
sources.claim_summary: LGBTQ+ news report (September 2021): under direct European Commission funding pressure, Lubelskie voivodeship repealed its 'LGBT-free' resolution on 20 September 2021 alongside two siblings, joining an earlier wave - EU demands, not changed conviction, drove the rescissions.

sources.title: Poland’s LGBT-Free Zones: From Declaration to Repeal - LegalClarity
sources.claim_summary: Legal-overview article on the rise and fall of Poland's LGBT-free zones: between 2019 and 2025 more than 100 local governments adopted 'LGBT ideology'-free resolutions or Ordo Iuris-drafted family-rights charters covering roughly a third of the country at peak; the documents created no criminal penalties but symbolically sidelined LGBT residents from civic life; the national human-rights commissioner's litigation led courts to strike them down as unconstitutional, the EU threatened to freeze billions in regional funds, and the last remaining zone was abolished in spring 2025.
